reasoning_traces.think:
The paper demonstrates that the Taylor expansion and GBM-based approximations to the Kelly criterion yield incorrect stake fractions, particularly in scenarios with skewed payoffs. For example, in Gamble A, both approximations suggest full-stake betting (K=1), yet the true optimum is only K*=0.6667, resulting in a positive growth rate of ~4% instead of a negative ~1.7%. This discrepancy arises because the approximations assume Gaussianity and ignore higher moments. The drawdown implications are severe: full Kelly in the coin-flip gamble leads to a 92% chance of exceeding 98% drawdown, whereas the constrained Kelly solution reduces this risk significantly. These insights necessitate replacing naive approximations with exact convex optimization under explicit drawdown constraints.
